pages.text: Madam Kumi put a Veronica bucket outside the school toilets. It was a big bucket of clean water with a small tap near the bottom. Beside it, she put a bar of soap and a bowl to catch the water.
sentences: Madam Kumi put a Veronica bucket outside the school toilets.
It was a big bucket of clean water with a small tap near the bottom.
Beside it, she put a bar of soap and a bowl to catch the water.
pages.alt: On a sunny Ghanaian school veranda, Madam Kumi sets up a blue plastic Veronica bucket with a bottom tap on a metal stand, a soap dish, and a catch-bowl below.

pages.text: After play, Akuffo ran to the bucket. He held his hands under the tap for one second. “Done!” he said. “Water is enough.” Madam Kumi smiled. “Water helps, but soap lifts the germs off. Let me show you.”
sentences: After play, Akuffo ran to the bucket.
He held his hands under the tap for one second.

“Water helps, but soap lifts the germs off.

pages.alt: Akuffo quickly dipping his fingertips under the small tap of the blue Veronica bucket for a moment while Madam Kumi smiles gently beside him.

pages.text: “First, wet your hands,” said Madam Kumi. “Then rub on soap. Scrub the backs of your hands, between your fingers and under your nails. Scrub for as long as it takes to sing a short song twice.” Dari sang as she scrubbed.
sentences: “First, wet your hands,” said Madam Kumi.
“Then rub on soap.
Scrub the backs of your hands, between your fingers and under your nails.
Scrub for as long as it takes to sing a short song twice.” Dari sang as she scrubbed.
pages.alt: Dari happily singing and rubbing rich white soapy lather between her fingers beside the Veronica bucket stand while Madam Kumi and Akuffo watch.

pages.text: “Now rinse your hands under the running water,” said Madam Kumi. “Dry them with a clean cloth or shake them in the air.” The dirty water ran into the bowl. Dari poured it into a drain and kept the area clean.
sentences: “Now rinse your hands under the running water,” said Madam Kumi.

pages.alt: Dari rinsing clean soapy water off her hands under the Veronica bucket tap into the catch-basin below on the tidy school veranda.

pages.text: “When must we wash our hands?” asked Madam Kumi. Akuffo answered, “Before we eat, after we use the toilet, and after we play outside.” “Yes,” she said, “and after we cough or sneeze into our hands, or touch animals.”
sentences: “When must we wash our hands?” asked Madam Kumi.
Akuffo answered, “Before we eat, after we use the toilet, and after we play outside.” “Yes,” she said, “and after we cough or sneeze into our hands, or touch animals.”
pages.alt: In the classroom, Akuffo raises his hand eagerly as Madam Kumi points to wordless picture icons showing mealtime, outdoor play, and petting a goat.

pages.text: From that day on, Dari and Akuffo washed their hands with soap at the Veronica bucket every time. “Clean hands keep us well,” said Dari. “And they keep our friends well, too,” said Akuffo. Madam Kumi gave them both a big smile.

pages.alt: Dari and Akuffo smiling brightly and holding up clean hands beside the blue Veronica bucket on the sunny school veranda as Madam Kumi beams.
